name: Kite
desc: A tethered wing of silk or paper on a frame, flown in ancient China; the first heavier-than-air craft.

name: Bamboo-copter
desc: A Chinese toy rotor spun by hand or string that flies upward; an early demonstration of rotary-wing lift.

name: Sky lantern
desc: A small paper hot-air balloon lifted by a flame, used in China for signalling; the principle behind the hot air balloon.

name: Hot air balloon
desc: The Montgolfier brothers' heated-air envelope that carried the first humans aloft in 1783.

name: Hydrogen balloon
desc: Jacques Charles's balloon filled with hydrogen, which floated longer and higher than hot air.

name: Parachute
desc: A canopy that slows descent through drag; André-Jacques Garnerin made the first jumps from a balloon in 1797.

name: Fixed-wing aircraft concept
desc: George Cayley's separation of lift, thrust and control, shown in his 1804 model glider; the basis of the airplane.

name: Aircraft propeller
desc: A rotating airfoil blade that converts engine power into thrust, first used on Giffard's 1852 airship.

name: Airship
desc: A steerable powered balloon; Henri Giffard flew a steam-driven one in 1852.

name: Glider
desc: An unpowered heavier-than-air craft; Cayley's 1853 glider carried a person across a valley.

name: Ornithopter
desc: A machine that flies by flapping wings; Gustave Trouvé's 1870 model was among the first to fly.

name: Wind tunnel
desc: A duct that blows air over models so lift and drag can be measured; first built by Francis Wenham in 1871.

name: Cambered airfoil
desc: A curved wing section, patented by Horatio Phillips in 1884, that produces far more lift than a flat plate.

name: De Laval nozzle
desc: A converging-diverging nozzle that accelerates gas to supersonic speed; the standard shape of rocket nozzles.

name: Lilienthal glider
desc: Otto Lilienthal's hang glider, flown hundreds of times; the first aircraft built in series and a model for the Wrights.

name: Biplane
desc: A two-wing layout braced as a truss, strong and light; used by Chanute's glider and the Wright Flyer.

name: Wing warping
desc: Twisting the wingtips to control roll, devised by the Wright brothers in 1899.

name: Rigid airship
desc: Ferdinand von Zeppelin's airship with a metal framework holding gas cells; used for the first airline service in 1910.

name: Tsiolkovsky rocket equation
desc: Konstantin Tsiolkovsky's relation between exhaust velocity, mass ratio and speed gain; the foundation of astronautics.

name: Aircraft engine
desc: A light, powerful piston engine built for flight; the Wrights' aluminium-block engine made powered flight possible.

name: Wright Flyer
desc: The Wright brothers' biplane that made the first controlled, sustained powered flight on 17 December 1903.

name: Pulsejet
desc: A simple jet engine with intermittent combustion behind valves; later used in the V-1 flying bomb.

name: Monoplane
desc: An aircraft with a single main wing; Louis Blériot's monoplanes set the layout used by most later aircraft.

name: Aileron
desc: A hinged control surface at the wing's trailing edge for roll control; replaced wing warping.

name: Rotary aircraft engine
desc: An air-cooled engine whose cylinders spin around a fixed crankshaft; the Gnome engine powered early aviation.

name: Blériot XI
desc: Louis Blériot's monoplane that made the first flight across the English Channel in 1909.

name: Airport
desc: A dedicated field with runways and services for aircraft; College Park, Maryland, opened in 1909.

name: Seaplane
desc: An aircraft that takes off from and lands on water; Henri Fabre flew the first in 1910.

name: Monocoque fuselage
desc: A fuselage whose skin carries the loads, introduced on the 1912 Deperdussin racer; led to stressed-skin aircraft.

name: Autopilot
desc: Lawrence Sperry's gyroscopic system that held an aircraft level and on course without pilot input.

name: Airliner
desc: A large aircraft for carrying passengers; Sikorsky's four-engine Russky Vityaz of 1913 pioneered the type.

name: All-metal aircraft
desc: Hugo Junkers's J 1, the first practical all-metal airplane, with an unbraced cantilever wing.

name: Flap
desc: A hinged trailing-edge surface that raises lift at low speed, allowing slower takeoffs and landings.

name: Unmanned aerial vehicle
desc: An aircraft without a pilot aboard, flown by radio or autopilot; first built as aerial targets and flying bombs in 1917.

name: Leading-edge slat
desc: A small airfoil ahead of the wing that delays stall; developed by Handley Page and Lachmann.

name: First nonstop transatlantic flight
wiki: Transatlantic flight of Alcock and Brown
desc: John Alcock and Arthur Brown's 1919 nonstop flight from Newfoundland to Ireland, proving long overwater flight.

name: Air traffic control
desc: Ground-based direction of aircraft to keep them separated; began at London's Croydon airport around 1920.

name: Retractable landing gear
desc: Wheels that fold into the aircraft in flight to cut drag; adopted widely from the Dayton-Wright RB-1 onward.

name: Aerial application
desc: Spraying crops with pesticides or fertilizer from aircraft; first done in Ohio in 1921.

name: Quadcopter
desc: A rotorcraft lifted by four rotors; early crewed versions flew in 1922, and electronic stabilization made them common drones.

name: Autogyro
desc: Juan de la Cierva's aircraft with a freely spinning rotor for lift; it introduced the hinged rotor blades used by helicopters.

name: Aerial refueling
desc: Transferring fuel from one aircraft to another in flight to extend range; first done by the US Army in 1923.

name: Variable-pitch propeller
desc: A propeller whose blade angle can change in flight for efficient takeoff and cruise.

name: Hohmann transfer orbit
desc: Walter Hohmann's fuel-efficient two-burn path between orbits, the basis of interplanetary mission design.

name: Flight simulator
desc: A ground device that reproduces flight for pilot training; Edwin Link's 1929 trainer was the first practical one.

name: Attitude indicator
desc: A gyroscopic artificial horizon that let pilots fly in cloud; key to Jimmy Doolittle's 1929 blind flight.

name: Delta wing
desc: A triangular wing, pioneered by Alexander Lippisch's gliders, suited to supersonic flight.

name: High-altitude balloon
desc: Auguste Piccard's balloon with a sealed gondola that carried people into the stratosphere in 1931.

name: Hybrid-propellant rocket
desc: A rocket burning a liquid oxidizer with a solid fuel; the Soviet GIRD-09 flew in 1933.

name: Pressure suit
desc: A sealed suit that keeps its wearer pressurized at high altitude; Wiley Post flew in one in 1934.

name: Douglas DC-3
desc: The all-metal airliner that made passenger air travel profitable and became the most widely used transport aircraft.

name: Helicopter
desc: A rotorcraft that lifts and steers with powered rotors; the Focke-Wulf Fw 61 of 1936 was the first fully controllable one.

name: Pressurized cabin
desc: Pumping air into a sealed fuselage so aircraft can fly above the weather; first on the Lockheed XC-35.

name: Instrument landing system
desc: Radio beams that guide aircraft down to the runway in poor visibility.

name: Turbojet
desc: A jet engine whose entire thrust comes from exhaust; the Heinkel He 178 made the first jet-powered flight in 1939.

name: Ramjet
desc: A jet engine with no moving parts that compresses air by forward speed alone; first flight-tested in the USSR in 1939.

name: Inertial navigation system
desc: Gyroscopes and accelerometers that track position without outside references; first used to guide the V-2.

name: Composite solid propellant
desc: Oxidizer crystals bound in a rubbery fuel, developed at GALCIT; the basis of large modern solid rocket motors.

name: Turbopump
desc: A turbine-driven pump that feeds propellant into a rocket engine at high pressure; made large liquid rockets possible.

name: V-2 rocket
desc: The first large guided liquid-fuel rocket and the first object to reach space, in 1944; it seeded postwar rocketry.

name: Ejection seat
desc: A seat that fires the pilot clear of a disabled aircraft before a parachute opens.

name: Sikorsky R-4
desc: The first helicopter built in quantity, using Igor Sikorsky's single main rotor and tail rotor layout.

name: Afterburner
desc: Extra fuel burned in a jet's exhaust for a short burst of thrust; used by supersonic aircraft.

name: Turboprop
desc: A gas turbine driving a propeller, efficient at medium speeds; first flown on the Gloster Trent Meteor.

name: Sounding rocket
desc: A research rocket that carries instruments on a brief suborbital flight; the WAC Corporal was an early example.

name: VHF omnidirectional range
desc: Ground radio beacons that give aircraft their bearing, forming the airway network for decades.

name: Swept wing
desc: A wing angled back to delay shock waves near the speed of sound, standard on jet aircraft.

name: Bell X-1
desc: The rocket plane in which Chuck Yeager made the first supersonic level flight in 1947.

name: Animals in space
desc: Fruit flies, monkeys and dogs flown on rockets to test whether living things could survive spaceflight.

name: Rogallo wing
desc: Francis Rogallo's flexible fabric wing, which led to the modern hang glider.

name: Multistage rocket
desc: A rocket that drops spent stages to reach higher speeds; Bumper, a V-2 with a WAC Corporal upper stage, flew in 1949.

name: Jet airliner
desc: A passenger aircraft powered by jet engines; the de Havilland Comet first flew in 1949 and halved travel times.

name: Turboshaft
desc: A gas turbine built to drive a shaft rather than make thrust; it transformed helicopter power and payload.

name: Variable-sweep wing
desc: A wing that pivots to change sweep in flight, first flown on the Bell X-5 in 1951.

name: Area rule
desc: Richard Whitcomb's rule for shaping aircraft to cut drag near the speed of sound.

name: VTOL aircraft
desc: Fixed-wing aircraft that take off and land vertically, using jet lift or tilting rotors; later the Harrier.

name: Tiltrotor
desc: An aircraft with rotors that tilt from vertical lift to forward flight; the Bell XV-3 first converted in 1958.

name: Boeing 707
desc: The swept-wing jet airliner that began the jet age of mass air travel.

name: Flight recorder
desc: A crash-proof recorder of flight data and cockpit sounds, devised by David Warren after Comet accidents.

name: R-7 rocket
desc: Sergei Korolev's rocket with strap-on boosters, the first ICBM and launcher of Sputnik, Vostok and Soyuz.

name: Sputnik 1
desc: The first artificial satellite, launched by the USSR on 4 October 1957, which began the Space Age.

name: Atmospheric entry heat shield
desc: Blunt and ablative heat shields that let a vehicle survive returning through the atmosphere from space.

name: Spacecraft solar panels
desc: Solar cells powering spacecraft, first on Vanguard 1; they let satellites run for years.

name: Communications satellite
desc: A satellite that relays radio, TV and phone signals; SCORE in 1958 and Telstar in 1962 were early ones.

name: Explorer 1
desc: The first US satellite, which discovered the Van Allen radiation belts.

name: Head-up display
desc: A transparent display that projects flight data into the pilot's view.

name: North American X-15
desc: A rocket plane that reached Mach 6.7 and the edge of space, testing hypersonic flight and reaction controls.

name: Space probe
desc: An uncrewed spacecraft sent beyond Earth orbit; Luna 1, 2 and 3 reached the Moon in 1959.

name: Gravity assist
desc: Using a planet's gravity to change a probe's speed and path; first used by Luna 3 in 1959.

name: Nuclear thermal rocket
desc: A rocket that heats hydrogen in a fission reactor; ground-tested in the Kiwi and NERVA programs.

name: Weather satellite
desc: A satellite that images clouds and measures the atmosphere; TIROS-1 sent the first TV pictures of weather in 1960.

name: Transit navigation satellite
desc: The first satellite navigation system, using Doppler shift to fix positions of ships and submarines.

name: Earth observation satellite
desc: A satellite that images Earth's surface; the Corona spy satellites first returned film from orbit in 1960.

name: Space capsule
desc: A blunt crewed or animal-carrying spacecraft that returns by heat shield and parachute; first recovered in 1960.

name: Turbofan
desc: A jet engine that drives a large fan to push extra air around the core, quieter and more efficient than a turbojet.

name: Space suit
desc: A pressurized garment that keeps astronauts alive in vacuum; first worn by Yuri Gagarin.

name: Vostok 1
desc: The flight that made Yuri Gagarin the first human in space and in orbit, on 12 April 1961.

name: Radioisotope thermoelectric generator
desc: A generator that turns heat from radioactive decay into electricity, powering probes far from the Sun.

name: Staged combustion cycle
desc: A rocket engine cycle that burns turbine exhaust in the main chamber for high efficiency; pioneered in the USSR.

name: Human-powered aircraft
desc: An aircraft flown by the pilot's muscle power; the Gossamer Albatross crossed the English Channel in 1979.

name: Jet pack
desc: A backpack thruster for individual flight; the Bell Rocket Belt first flew freely in 1961.

name: Project Mercury
desc: The first US human spaceflight program; Alan Shepard flew in 1961 and John Glenn orbited in 1962.

name: Mariner 2
desc: The first successful planetary flyby, passing Venus in 1962.

name: Cryogenic rocket engine
desc: An engine burning liquid hydrogen and oxygen for the highest chemical efficiency; the RL10 first flew in 1963.

name: Deep Space Network
desc: A worldwide array of large antennas that tracks and talks to distant spacecraft.

name: Geostationary satellite
desc: A satellite that orbits in step with Earth's rotation and appears fixed in the sky; Syncom 3 was the first.

name: Ion thruster
desc: An engine that accelerates ions electrically for very efficient, low thrust; tested on SERT-1 in 1964.

name: High-bypass turbofan
desc: The GE TF39, first high-bypass turbofan, which made wide-body aircraft economical.

name: Parafoil
desc: Domina Jalbert's ram-air inflated fabric wing, the basis of steerable parachutes and paragliders.

name: Extravehicular activity
desc: Working outside a spacecraft in a space suit; Alexei Leonov made the first spacewalk in 1965.

name: Space rendezvous
desc: Bringing two spacecraft together in orbit, first done by Gemini 6A and 7 in 1965.

name: Mariner 4
desc: The first successful flyby of Mars, returning the first close-up pictures of another planet.

name: Spacecraft docking
desc: Physically joining two spacecraft in orbit, first done by Gemini 8 with an Agena target in 1966.

name: Luna 9
desc: The first spacecraft to soft-land on the Moon and send pictures from its surface.

name: Apollo Guidance Computer
desc: The compact integrated-circuit computer that navigated the Apollo spacecraft to the Moon.

name: Soyuz spacecraft
desc: A three-person Soviet spacecraft, still flying, which became the longest-serving crewed vehicle.

name: Saturn V
desc: The three-stage super heavy rocket that launched the Apollo Moon missions.

name: Apollo Lunar Module
desc: The two-stage lander that carried astronauts from lunar orbit to the surface and back.

name: Space telescope
desc: A telescope in orbit, above the blurring and absorbing atmosphere; OAO-2 was the first successful one.

name: Supersonic transport
desc: An airliner that cruises faster than sound; the Tupolev Tu-144 flew first, in 1968.

name: Apollo 8
desc: The first crewed spacecraft to leave Earth orbit and circle the Moon, in December 1968.

name: Apollo 11 Moon landing
desc: The mission that landed Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the Moon on 20 July 1969.

name: Concorde
desc: The Anglo-French supersonic airliner that crossed the Atlantic in under 3.5 hours from 1976 to 2003.

name: Wide-body aircraft
desc: A twin-aisle airliner that cut the cost per seat and opened long-haul flying to mass travel.

name: Boeing 747
desc: The first wide-body jumbo jet, which dominated long-haul air travel for decades.

name: Venera 7
desc: The first spacecraft to land on another planet, Venus, and transmit data from its surface.

name: Lunokhod 1
desc: The first robotic rover on another world, driven remotely across the Moon.

name: Sample return mission
desc: A robotic mission that brings material back to Earth; Luna 16 returned lunar soil in 1970.

name: Salyut space station
desc: The Soviet Salyut 1, the first space station, followed by a series of long-duration orbital outposts.

name: Hall-effect thruster
desc: An electric thruster that traps electrons in a magnetic field to ionize propellant; common on modern satellites.

name: Supercritical airfoil
desc: A flattened wing section by Richard Whitcomb that delays drag rise near the speed of sound.

name: Lunar Roving Vehicle
desc: A battery-powered car driven by astronauts on the Moon during the last three Apollo missions.

name: Mariner 9
desc: The first spacecraft to orbit another planet, mapping Mars in 1971 and 1972.

name: Pioneer 10
desc: The first probe to cross the asteroid belt and fly past Jupiter.

name: Landsat
desc: The longest-running civilian Earth imaging program, mapping land use, crops and forests since 1972.

name: Fly-by-wire
desc: Flight controls run by computers and wires instead of cables; NASA's F-8 first flew digital fly-by-wire in 1972.

name: Electric aircraft
desc: An aircraft driven by electric motors; the battery-powered MB-E1 made the first crewed electric flight in 1973.

name: Skylab
desc: The first US space station, built from a Saturn V stage, which hosted three crews in 1973 and 1974.

name: Ground proximity warning system
desc: A system that warns pilots when an aircraft is in danger of flying into terrain.

name: Viking Mars landers
desc: The first fully successful landings on Mars, which studied its surface and searched for life.

name: Voyager program
desc: Two probes that toured the outer planets; Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012.

name: Stealth aircraft
desc: Aircraft shaped and coated to be hard to detect by radar, first demonstrated by Have Blue in 1977.

name: Global Positioning System
desc: A constellation of satellites broadcasting precise time signals so receivers anywhere can find their position.

name: Progress cargo spacecraft
desc: An uncrewed automated freighter that resupplies space stations, enabling long-duration crews.

name: Winglet
desc: Upturned wingtips that reduce induced drag and fuel burn, flight-tested by NASA in 1979.

name: Space Shuttle
desc: NASA's partly reusable winged orbiter, which flew 135 missions from 1981 to 2011.

name: Canadarm
desc: A robotic arm on the Space Shuttle for deploying and capturing payloads.

name: Glass cockpit
desc: Electronic screens replacing mechanical cockpit gauges, first on the Boeing 767 and Airbus A310.

name: GLONASS
desc: Russia's global satellite navigation system, the second fully global one after GPS.

name: Mir
desc: The first modular space station, assembled in orbit and crewed almost continuously for ten years.

name: Airbus A320
desc: The first airliner with digital fly-by-wire and side-stick controls, and one of the best-selling jets.

name: Buran
desc: The Soviet reusable orbiter that made a single uncrewed orbital flight and automatic landing in 1988.

name: Hubble Space Telescope
desc: A large optical telescope in orbit, serviced by astronauts, that reshaped astronomy.

name: Traffic collision avoidance system
desc: An onboard system that interrogates nearby transponders and tells pilots how to avoid mid-air collisions.

name: Scramjet
desc: A ramjet with supersonic airflow through the combustor, for hypersonic flight; first flight-tested in 1991.

name: Vertical landing rocket
desc: Rockets that take off and land vertically on their engines; the DC-X demonstrated it in 1993.

name: Galileo spacecraft
desc: The first spacecraft to orbit Jupiter, which also dropped a probe into its atmosphere in 1995.

name: Mars rover
desc: A robotic vehicle that drives across Mars; Sojourner was the first to operate there, in 1997.

name: International Space Station
desc: A multinational modular station, continuously crewed since 2000, the largest structure in orbit.

name: Iridium satellite constellation
desc: A network of 66 low-orbit satellites giving phone coverage everywhere on Earth.

name: Chandra X-ray Observatory
desc: A space telescope with nested grazing-incidence mirrors that images the X-ray sky in fine detail.

name: BeiDou
desc: China's satellite navigation system, regional from 2000 and global from 2020.

name: Space tourism
desc: Paid private travel to space, beginning with Dennis Tito's visit to the ISS in 2001.

name: CubeSat
desc: A standard satellite built from 10 cm cubes, which made spaceflight affordable for universities and startups.

name: Shenzhou 5
desc: China's first crewed spaceflight, carrying Yang Liwei to orbit in 2003.

name: SpaceShipOne
desc: The first privately developed crewed spacecraft to reach space, winning the Ansari X Prize in 2004.

name: Cassini-Huygens
desc: A mission that orbited Saturn for 13 years and landed the Huygens probe on Titan in 2005.

name: NASA X-43
desc: An uncrewed scramjet test vehicle that reached Mach 9.6 in 2004, the fastest air-breathing flight.

name: Airbus A380
desc: A full-length double-deck airliner, the largest passenger aircraft ever built.

name: Boeing 787 Dreamliner
desc: The first airliner with a mostly carbon-fiber composite airframe, cutting weight and fuel use.

name: Solar Impulse
desc: A solar-electric aircraft that flew around the world without fuel in 2015 and 2016.

name: Kepler space telescope
desc: A space telescope that found thousands of exoplanets by watching stars dim as planets crossed them.

name: Falcon 9
desc: SpaceX's two-stage medium-lift rocket, which became the most-flown launcher in the world.

name: Hayabusa
desc: A Japanese ion-propelled probe that returned the first samples from an asteroid in 2010.

name: Solar sail
desc: A large thin sail pushed by sunlight; Japan's IKAROS first demonstrated it between planets in 2010.

name: SpaceX Dragon
desc: The first commercial spacecraft recovered from orbit, later the first to deliver cargo to the ISS.

name: eVTOL aircraft
desc: Battery-electric aircraft that take off vertically with many rotors, developed as air taxis; Volocopter flew first in 2011.

name: Galileo navigation system
desc: The European Union's civilian global satellite navigation system, with its first operational satellites in 2011.

name: Curiosity rover
desc: A car-sized nuclear-powered Mars rover lowered by a rocket sky crane in 2012.

name: Rosetta
desc: The first spacecraft to orbit a comet, which landed the Philae probe on its surface in 2014.

name: Reusable orbital booster
desc: A first stage that lands itself for reuse; a Falcon 9 booster first landed after an orbital launch in December 2015.

name: New Horizons
desc: The probe that made the first flyby of Pluto in 2015.

name: New Shepard
desc: Blue Origin's suborbital rocket, the first booster to fly to space and land vertically, in November 2015.

name: Delivery drone
desc: An uncrewed aircraft that carries packages; Zipline began regular medical deliveries in Rwanda in 2016.

name: Parker Solar Probe
desc: A heat-shielded probe that flies through the Sun's corona, the fastest object ever built.

name: Electron rocket
desc: A small launcher with 3D-printed, battery-pumped engines, dedicated to launching small satellites.

name: Raptor engine
desc: The first full-flow staged combustion engine to fly, burning methane and liquid oxygen.

name: Starlink
desc: A constellation of thousands of low-orbit satellites providing broadband internet worldwide.

name: Crew Dragon
desc: The first commercially built and operated spacecraft to carry astronauts to orbit, in 2020.

name: Hayabusa2
desc: A Japanese probe that returned samples from asteroid Ryugu in 2020, including material from below its surface.

name: Tiangong space station
desc: China's modular space station, assembled from 2021 and permanently crewed.

name: Perseverance rover
desc: A Mars rover caching rock cores for future return to Earth; it landed in Jezero Crater in 2021.

name: Ingenuity helicopter
desc: A small solar-charged helicopter that made the first powered flight on another planet, on Mars in 2021.

name: James Webb Space Telescope
desc: A large infrared space telescope with a folding segmented mirror, observing the earliest galaxies.

name: DART
desc: The first test of planetary defense, which changed an asteroid's orbit by deliberately crashing into it.

name: Artemis program
desc: NASA's program to return humans to the Moon, starting with the uncrewed Artemis I flight in 2022.

name: Starship
desc: The largest rocket ever flown, designed for full reuse; its booster was first caught by the launch tower in 2024.

name: OSIRIS-REx
desc: NASA's first asteroid sample return, bringing material from asteroid Bennu to Earth in 2023.

name: Chandrayaan-3
desc: India's first soft landing on the Moon, and the first near its south polar region, in 2023.

name: Chang'e 6
desc: A Chinese mission that returned the first samples from the far side of the Moon in 2024.
